clue.text: Arnold's dead hero leads the sprint? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the hero goes in front of the race, so his name comes first

parts.note: Matthew Arnold's poem Balder Dead is about the Norse god Balder
a sprint is a dash

explanation.surface: A sports report: the fallen hero of a poem heads the field in a short race.
explanation.walkthrough: BALDER is the subject of Matthew Arnold's narrative poem Balder Dead; 'leads' puts him before DASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Beast tips the plate over

indicators.note: with over, to tip something over is to turn it upside down, so the word is read backwards
completes 'tips over', the signal to read the plate word backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A clumsy creature knocks a dinner plate over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips ... over' turns LAMINA, a thin plate, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, an animal.

clue.text: Conservative types with fast views

parts.note: people who hold firmly ('fast') to old opinions, the stubborn resisters of change, a name also once given to an old British regiment

explanation.definitionFit: Die-hards are those who cling obstinately to traditional views.

clue.text: The fertile gramophone?

parts.note: a gramophone plays records back, and something fertile breeds offspring: both make copies

explanation.definitionFit: The sound box of an old gramophone was called this, and a creature that breeds is one too.

clue.text: Pardon my confession of broodiness?

definitions.meaning: a broody hen might confess 'I ...', i.e. inclined to sit on a nest

explanation.definitionFit: A state pardon for a class of offenders, and, split up, a hen's admission of wanting to nest.

clue.text: Darn — one needs the knack

definitions.meaning: to get the ... of something is to acquire the knack

explanation.surface: A mender who must have the skill to darn socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild curse like 'blast', and the skill or trick of doing something.

clue.text: Cheated all round — cheat forgiven

indicators.note: the first word's synonym goes all round the second's, enclosing it

parts.note: conned means cheated
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: Swindled on every side, the swindler is let off.
explanation.definitionFit: Condoned means overlooked or pardoned an offence.

clue.text: Mrs Grundy put in mince-pie — that wasn't wise

indicators.note: the narrow-minded lady is placed inside the jumbled letters
printer's pie is type jumbled together, so the preceding word is mixed up

parts.note: Mrs Grundy, from an old play, stands for a censorious prude

explanation.surface: A prim old lady is stuffed into a Christmas pie, an unwise move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' (as in printer's pie, jumbled type) mixes MINCE to IMNCE; 'put in' places PRUDE inside it after IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudence is rashness, behaviour lacking good sense.

clue.text: Like Nanki-Poo's Flowers, giving a good time without money

indicators.note: here means outside, so the first pieces surround the money

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Garden praise in operetta style: blooms that give pleasure without costing a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado, Nanki-Poo sings of 'the flowers that bloom in the spring'. 'without' means outside: A BOOM wraps L.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's flowers are in flower, blossoming.

clue.text: Fair point — joke is too subtle

parts.note: fine weather is fair weather
S, south, is a point of the compass
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A critic grants the point is fair but finds the gag overly clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun means delicately drawn out, excessively refined.

clue.text: Father is one who finishes — latest to come in

indicators.note: the news is put inside the finisher

parts.note: an ender ends things
gen is slang for the latest information

explanation.surface: Dad is the one who completes the job, the last to arrive home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come in' puts GEN inside ENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To father is to beget, bring into being.

clue.text: Like a flapper after the king

parts.note: French 'à la', in the manner of, is a sense of 'after'
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A 1920s girl dancing in the style of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' in the sense 'in the style of' is A LA, as in à la mode.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar means relating to wings, and a flapper is a wing.

clue.text: Nude (what with one thing and another)

definitions.text: what with one thing and another
definitions.meaning: taking everything together, on the whole

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in the altogether' means naked, and the word also means in total, considering everything.

clue.text: Defined as a backward chap in fur

indicators.note: the chap's name is to be read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
ermined means trimmed or clad in ermine fur

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gone odd: a fellow walking backwards in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns TED into DET, followed by ERMINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined can mean fixed or settled exactly, specified.

clue.text: Noisy, like Hamlet's periwig-pated fellow

definitions.meaning: Hamlet scorns 'a ... periwig-pated fellow' who rants on stage

explanation.definitionFit: An old word for boisterous and rough, used by Hamlet of an overacting player.

clue.text: How to divide the rations of Jerome's boatmen, for instance?

definitions.text: How to divide the rations of Jerome's boatmen, for instance?

parts.words: How to divide the rations of Jerome's boatmen, for instance?
parts.note: Jerome K Jerome wrote Three Men in a Boat, so food shared among his crew is cut into three equal parts

explanation.definitionFit: To cut into three equal portions.

clue.text: Takes pleasure, many note, in swirling undies

indicators.note: the two short pieces go inside the jumbled underwear
the underwear is whirled about, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys watching underwear spin in the washing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns UNDIES into INDUES; 'in' sets L and G inside after INDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge is to gratify oneself or enjoy freely.

clue.text: The devil — a worthless fellow

parts.note: bad means worthless
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Calling some scoundrel a no-good devil.
explanation.walkthrough: Abaddon is a name for Satan or hell in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaddon is the biblical angel of the bottomless pit, Satan.

clue.text: Every girl's standing as the guard comes out

indicators.note: the words emerge in a new order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A young lady stands to attention while the sentry marches out.
explanation.definitionFit: Every girl is somebody's female child, a relation she holds from birth.

clue.text: Where a glamour girl must excel, to succeed

definitions.text: Where a glamour girl must excel
definitions.meaning: split up, it means '...', 'it' being slang for sex appeal
to succeed as heir, come into property

explanation.surface: A model's career depends on having star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into a legacy as successor, and, read as three words, having sex appeal.

clue.text: Church nomenclators

parts.note: a nomenclator gives names; at a christening those sponsoring the infant answer for its name

explanation.definitionFit: Sponsors at a baptism, who name the child in church.

clue.text: " Or — the flying ball " (Gray)

parts.note: a line from Thomas Gray's Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College with a word missing: the boys drive on the ball

explanation.definitionFit: Gray's line reads 'Or impel the rolling circle's speed, Or ...the flying ball', the verb meaning to drive onward.

clue.text: Sand in aircraft's control?

definitions.meaning: ... Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
pilots nicknamed the automatic pilot this

explanation.surface: Grit has got into a plane's controls.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's male pen name, and RAF slang for the autopilot.

clue.text: Revealing a measure in dry drink

indicators.note: the measure goes inside the teetotal letters

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
an ell is an old measure of length
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A drinker's tip: the amount poured into a dry drink gives things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ELL inside TT; ALE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Telltale signs are those that betray or disclose something.

clue.text: Sounds a smart lad

parts.note: a know-all is called a 'smart' plus this boy's name

explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a cocky know-all, so the name completes the phrase.

clue.text: Birds with supporters round South

indicators.note: the supporters go round the compass point

parts.note: rooters are fans who root for a team

explanation.surface: Fans flock around the southern stand like birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosters are cockerels, male chickens.

clue.text: Issue backed by, for example, army technicians

indicators.note: everything after it is read in reverse order

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A matter supported by the army's mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out, appear.

clue.text: A secret tot, concealed in a conspiratorial way

indicators.note: the letters are disguised, their order hidden by rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a hidden nip of spirits like a plotter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' rearranges A SECRET TOT. Cato Street in London gave its name to the 1820 plot to murder the Cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a way, and this one housed the 1820 conspirators.
